title: Pointer
description: Unified mouse / touch / pen pointer. Wraps a single browser `PointerEvent.pointerId` and writes its state (position, buttons, pressure, tilt, etc.) into the engine's shared channels buffer so it can be polled by Input bindings or read directly by interaction-aware scene nodes. Coordinates are stored in logical/design pixel space — i.e. `app.width`/ `app.height` units (`0..app.width` × `0..app.height`), matching node positions, the 2-argument View.screenToWorld, and the active camera. The CSS-pixel event coordinates are mapped through the application's content viewport, so the value is independent of Application.pixelRatio and of however the canvas is displayed (sizingMode `'fit'`/`'shrink'`/`'letterbox'`, or a CSS transform): a click at the right edge always reads `app.width`. In `'letterbox'` mode the letterbox bars map outside `0..app.width`. The channel writes are normalized to 0..1 (position, size, twist, tilt) for backend-agnostic sampling. Pointers are owned by the InputManager, which assigns them a slot index in 0..15 (see maxPointers) and exposes their per-slot channel offsets via the Pointer class namespace constants.

members.name: new
members.signature: new(event: PointerEvent, app: Application, platform: PlatformAdapter, channels: Float32Array, slotIndex: number): Pointer

members.name: cancelPosition
members.description: Position the platform cancelled this pointer at. (-1, -1) until it has been cancelled at least once.

members.name: delta
members.description: Movement accumulated over the current frame — position - previousPosition.

members.name: movePosition
members.description: Position of the most recent move. Several platform moves in one frame collapse into this, their last one — the coordinates the frame's moved phase is dispatched at. (-1, -1) until the pointer has moved at least once.

members.name: position
members.description: Current position in design pixels — always the pointer's latest, live position, never rewound to an earlier phase. A signal handler that needs the coordinates a SPECIFIC phase happened at (press, move, release, context menu) receives them as explicit arguments rather than reading this property, and InteractionEvent.x/InteractionEvent.y are the corresponding immutable per-phase snapshot at the interaction layer — this is a deliberate choice over a temporary rewind-and-restore, which could leave a handler reading a DIFFERENT phase's position if it runs any code after the dispatch that called it returns.

members.name: pressPosition
members.description: Position of the most recent press. Retains its value after release so tap/drag logic can still read it.

members.name: previousPosition
members.description: Position at the previous frame boundary. Together with position it spans delta: position - previousPosition === delta on any frame read outside a phase dispatch.

members.name: releasePosition
members.description: Position of the most recent release. (-1, -1) until the pointer has been released at least once.

members.name: cancelled
members.description: true when the platform cancelled this pointer during this frame (system gesture, focus loss, …).

members.name: down
members.description: true while at least one button is held. Reflects the live button state, not a frame phase.

members.name: entered
members.description: true when the pointer entered the canvas during this frame.

members.name: exited
members.description: true when the pointer left the canvas during this frame.

members.name: maxDistanceFromPress
members.description: Largest distance the pointer reached from pressPosition during the current press, in design pixels. Accumulated from every platform move, so a pointer that travels far and returns to its press position does *not* read as a tap. Resets on the next press.

members.name: moved
members.description: true when the pointer moved during this frame. Several platform moves collapse into one.

members.name: pressed
members.description: true when the pointer was pressed during this frame. A press and release that both land between two frames set pressed *and* released on the same frame — the phases are not lost.

members.name: released
members.description: true when the pointer was released during this frame.
